title: A Solver-Free Training Method for Predict-then-Optimize
claim: Blind training is cheap but ignores the task, and decision-aware training needs a costly solver; ours gets task-awareness without the solver.
layout: 3 columns, top-to-bottom flow, ours in the center, shaded backgrounds
description: Three vertical columns show training pipelines as stacked colored boxes joined by arrows. Left, 'Decision-blind': Dataset (pink) goes by a Sample arrow to Model (orange), which exchanges Prediction and Gradient arrows with a Prediction Loss box (blue). Right, 'Decision-focused': the same Dataset and Model, but the Prediction and Gradient arrows pass through a dark teal Optimization Solver box and then a Decision Loss box. Middle, 'Our approach' on a lighter background: a Measure Transformation arrow turns Dataset into a dark red Transformed Dataset, which is sampled into Model and then Prediction Loss, with no solver. The red Transformed Dataset box is the only new element and draws the eye first. Colors are consistent across columns, so the differences stand out.
caption: Schematic comparison of training pipelines. (Left) Decision-blind learning minimizes prediction error without considering the downstream task. (Right) Decision-focused methods incorporate the optimization solver into the training loop, requiring computationally expensive differentiation through the solver. (Mid) Our approach integrates the optimization structure by a measure transformation, enabling a completely solver-free training process that maintains the computational efficiency of decision-blind methods while achieving decision-aware performance.
abstract: We propose a scalable method for training prediction (machine learning) models in the predict-then-optimize paradigm, where model outputs serve as coefficients for a subsequent linear optimization task. Directly minimizing the empirical decision regret is intractable for linear programming and combinatorial optimization since the decision mapping is piecewise constant, and the gradients are zero almost everywhere. While existing methods address this by smoothing the differentiation process, they suffer from scalability issues, since a computationally expensive solver call is required for every gradient evaluation. To address this, we propose a decision-focused learning pipeline based on a measure transformation principle, which yields a new surrogate loss that is completely optimization-solver-free during training. We establish theoretical guarantees, including Fisher consistency and excess risk bounds. Empirically, our method achieves decision quality competitive with state-of-the-art methods while reducing training time by orders of magnitude.
